Apple___Apple_scab.name: Apple Scab
Apple___Apple_scab.description: Apple scab is a serious disease of apple trees that affects both leaves and fruit, leading to aesthetic and yield losses.
Apple___Apple_scab.symptoms: Olive-green to black velvety spots on leaves; fruit develops brown, corky lesions or cracks.
Apple___Apple_scab.causes: Fungal pathogen that overwinter in fallen leaves and spreads via spring rains.
Apple___Apple_scab.treatment: Apply fungicides like copper or sulfur sprays during early bud break.
Apple___Apple_scab.prevention: Rake and destroy fallen leaves in autumn; prune trees to improve air circulation; plant resistant apple cultivars.

Apple___Black_rot.name: Apple Black Rot
Apple___Black_rot.description: A fungal disease causing cankers on limbs, frogeye leaf spots, and rotting of fruit.
Apple___Black_rot.symptoms: Small purple spots on leaves expanding into 'frogeye' spots; fruit rots with concentric rings and black pycnidia; bark cankers.
Apple___Black_rot.causes: Fungus overwintering in dead wood, mummified fruit, and bark cankers.
Apple___Black_rot.treatment: Prune out dead wood and cankers; apply appropriate fungicides from tight cluster stage through harvest.
Apple___Black_rot.prevention: Remove mummified fruit from trees; destroy infected wood; maintain tree vigor with proper fertilizing.

Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.name: Cedar Apple Rust
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.description: A heteroecious rust disease requiring both apple trees and Eastern Red Cedar hosts to complete its life cycle.
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.symptoms: Bright orange-yellow spots on upper leaf surfaces; tube-like projections (aecia) on the underside of leaves and fruit.
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.causes: Fungal spores blown from cedar galls to apple leaves during warm spring rains.
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.treatment: Apply preventive fungicides (e.g., myclobutanil) during the pink bud stage through petal fall.
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.prevention: Remove nearby cedar trees or prune cedar galls in winter; choose rust-resistant apple varieties.

Apple___healthy.name: Healthy Apple
Apple___healthy.description: The apple tree is healthy, displaying normal vigor, clean foliage, and healthy fruit growth.
Apple___healthy.symptoms: None. Leaves are green, intact, and free from spots or discoloration.
Apple___healthy.prevention: Continue standard cultural practices, including routine pruning, watering, and soil management.

Blueberry___healthy.name: Healthy Blueberry
Blueberry___healthy.description: The blueberry plant is healthy, showing bright foliage, normal growth, and healthy berry production.
Blueberry___healthy.symptoms: None. Green, clean foliage with standard growth behavior.
Blueberry___healthy.prevention: Maintain soil pH between 4.5 and 5.0, prune annually, and apply organic mulch.

Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.name: Cherry Powdery Mildew
Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.description: A common fungal disease affecting cherries, particularly young leaves and shoots, reducing photosynthesis.
Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.symptoms: White, powdery fungal patches on leaves and twigs; leaves curl upwards and become distorted.
Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.causes: Fungus that thrives in high humidity and moderate temperatures, spreading via wind.
Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.treatment: Apply sulfur or potassium bicarbonate fungicides at first sign of disease.
Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.prevention: Prune trees to open the canopy; avoid overhead watering; remove suckers from the base.

Cherry_(including_sour)___healthy.name: Healthy Cherry
Cherry_(including_sour)___healthy.description: The cherry tree is healthy, showcasing clean leaves, solid structure, and healthy fruit production.
Cherry_(including_sour)___healthy.symptoms: None. Foliage is green, glossy, and free of spots or fungal dust.
Cherry_(including_sour)___healthy.prevention: Follow annual pruning routines, apply organic compost, and monitor for pests.

Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.name: Corn Gray Leaf Spot
Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.description: A major fungal disease of corn causing significant foliar damage and crop yield loss in warm, humid areas.
Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.symptoms: Rectangular, tan-to-gray leaf spots restricted by leaf veins, resembling matches.
Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.causes: Fungal pathogen that overwinters in corn crop residue on the soil surface.
Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.treatment: Apply foliar fungicides (e.g., strobilurins or triazoles) if disease pressure is high before tasseling.
Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.prevention: Rotate crops with non-hosts like soybeans; practice tillage to bury residue; plant resistant corn hybrids.

Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.name: Corn Common Rust
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.description: A fungal rust disease that attacks corn, characterized by powdery brick-red pustules on foliage.
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.symptoms: Oval, cinnamon-brown pustules on both upper and lower surfaces of leaves that erupt to release powdery spores.
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.causes: Fungal spores blown north from southern overwintering areas by spring winds.
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.treatment: Fungicide applications are rarely cost-effective unless severe rust occurs early on susceptible inbred lines.
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.prevention: Plant resistant hybrids; manage planting dates to avoid high spore concentrations.

Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.name: Corn Northern Leaf Blight
Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.description: A destructive fungal disease of corn characterized by large, cigar-shaped lesions on leaves.
Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.symptoms: Long, elliptical, grayish-green or tan lesions (1-6 inches long) starting on lower leaves.
Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.causes: Fungus overwintering in infected corn residues, spreading via wind and water splashes.
Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.treatment: Fungicides can be applied if symptoms appear early and weather conditions are favorable for disease spreads.
Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.prevention: Rotate crops; harvest/plow under old residues; select resistant hybrids.

Corn_(maize)___healthy.name: Healthy Corn
Corn_(maize)___healthy.description: The corn plant is healthy, showing thick green stalks and healthy foliage free of leaf blights.
Corn_(maize)___healthy.symptoms: None. Long leaves are uniform green, without stripe lesions or rust pustules.
Corn_(maize)___healthy.prevention: Follow crop rotation schedules, ensure balanced nitrogen levels, and manage soil drainage.

Grape___Black_rot.name: Grape Black Rot
Grape___Black_rot.description: A highly destructive grape fungal disease that destroys berries, leaves, and shoots, causing severe crop failure.
Grape___Black_rot.symptoms: Reddish-brown circular spots on leaves; berries turn brown, shrivel, and transform into hard, black mummies.
Grape___Black_rot.causes: Fungus overwintering in grape mummies on the vine or ground, activated by rain.
Grape___Black_rot.treatment: Apply fungicides containing mancozeb, ziram, or myclobutanil starting at bud break.
Grape___Black_rot.prevention: Remove all mummified fruit during winter pruning; prune shoots to keep vines off the ground; cultivate sun-exposed rows.

Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).name: Grape Esca (Black Measles)
Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).description: A complex wood-rot disease of grapevines causing leaf mottling, vine decline, and skin spots on berries.
Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).symptoms: Tiger-stripe leaf discoloration (chlorosis and necrosis); dark spots (measles) on berry skins; wood decay.
Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).causes: Fungi entering through pruning wounds and slowly colonizing the vascular system of the vine.
Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).treatment: Protect pruning wounds with sealants; remove and burn severely infected vines to protect the vineyard.
Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).prevention: Prune during dry winter periods; apply wound dressings; maintain good vine vigor.

Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.name: Grape Leaf Blight
Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.description: A fungal leaf disease causing premature defoliation in late summer, weakening grapevines.
Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.symptoms: Dark brown, irregular spots on leaves that merge, causing leaves to dry, curl up, and fall off early.
Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.causes: Fungus that overwinters on fallen leaves, spreading in wet, warm summer conditions.
Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.treatment: Apply protective copper or organic fungicides if disease appears mid-season.
Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.prevention: Rake and destroy fallen leaves; prune vines to maximize sun exposure and air flow.

Grape___healthy.name: Healthy Grape
Grape___healthy.description: The grapevine is healthy, displaying vibrant green leaves, strong shoots, and healthy clusters of grapes.
Grape___healthy.symptoms: None. Uniform green leaves with no necrotic borders or mummified berries.
Grape___healthy.prevention: Perform consistent canopy management, prune annually in late winter, and check soil nutrient levels.

Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).name: Citrus Greening (HLB)
Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).description: A devastating, incurable bacterial disease of citrus trees spread by insects, causing fruit to stay green and bitter.
Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).symptoms: Mottled yellow leaves; stunted tree growth; small, lopsided, bitter green fruit with dark seeds.
Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).causes: Bacterium transmitted by the Asian Citrus Psyllid (Diaphorina citri) insect vector.
Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).treatment: No cure exists. Infected trees must be removed and destroyed to prevent spreading the bacteria.
Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).prevention: Control psyllid populations with insecticides or natural predators; use certified disease-free nursery stock.

Peach___Bacterial_spot.name: Peach Bacterial Spot
Peach___Bacterial_spot.description: A bacterial disease affecting peach leaves, fruit, and twigs, resulting in defoliation and unmarketable fruit.
Peach___Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Small, water-soaked, purple-to-brown lesions on leaves that drop out, leaving a 'shot-hole' appearance; cracked fruit.
Peach___Bacterial_spot.causes: Bacterial pathogen that overwinters in twig cankers and spreads in warm, wet spring weather.
Peach___Bacterial_spot.treatment: Apply copper sprays or oxytetracycline during early spring and petal fall.
Peach___Bacterial_spot.prevention: Avoid planting susceptible cultivars; prune to facilitate rapid drying of leaves; avoid overhead irrigation.

Peach___healthy.name: Healthy Peach
Peach___healthy.description: The peach tree is healthy, displaying lush foliage, clean branches, and normal fruit development.
Peach___healthy.symptoms: None. Smooth, green leaves without shot-holes or bacterial spots.
Peach___healthy.prevention: Apply protective sprays during dormancy, prune trees into an open center shape, and keep tree surrounds clear.

Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.name: Pepper Bacterial Spot
Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.description: A serious bacterial disease causing leaf drop, fruit spot, and yield loss in bell peppers.
Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Small, dark, circular spots on leaves with yellow halos; raised, scab-like spots on peppers.
Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.causes: Bacterial pathogen carried on infected seed or surviving in crop residue, spread by rain splash.
Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.treatment: Spray copper-based bactericides at weekly intervals when conditions are hot and wet.
Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.prevention: Use certified pathogen-free seed; practice crop rotation; stay out of fields when foliage is wet.

Pepper,_bell___healthy.name: Healthy Pepper
Pepper,_bell___healthy.description: The bell pepper plant is healthy, showing upright growth, clean leaves, and shiny green fruit.
Pepper,_bell___healthy.symptoms: None. Clear, flat green leaves without dark spots or yellowing.
Pepper,_bell___healthy.prevention: Rotate pepper plantings with grass crops, apply mulch to prevent soil splashing, and irrigate at the soil level.

Potato___Early_blight.name: Potato Early Blight
Potato___Early_blight.description: A fungal disease of potato leaves characterized by dark spots with concentric 'target' rings.
Potato___Early_blight.symptoms: Dark brown-to-black spots on older leaves displaying concentric rings (target board pattern).
Potato___Early_blight.causes: Fungal pathogen that overwinters in plant debris and soil, spreading in alternating wet and dry conditions.
Potato___Early_blight.treatment: Apply fungicides (e.g., chlorothalonil or mancozeb) when early lesions appear on lower leaves.
Potato___Early_blight.prevention: Rotate crops; destroy crop residues after harvest; ensure proper nitrogen levels to reduce susceptibility.

Potato___Late_blight.name: Potato Late Blight
Potato___Late_blight.description: A destructive water-mold disease that can rapidly destroy entire potato crops in wet weather, famously causing the Irish Potato Famine.
Potato___Late_blight.symptoms: Large, dark, water-soaked lesions on leaves with white mold on the underside in humid conditions; tubers rot.
Potato___Late_blight.causes: Oomycete pathogen that spreads rapidly via airborne spores in cool, damp conditions.
Potato___Late_blight.treatment: Apply protective fungicides (e.g., metalaxyl or copper sprays) immediately on forecast of cool, wet weather.
Potato___Late_blight.prevention: Plant certified disease-free seed tubers; destroy volunteer potato plants; remove infected plants immediately.

Potato___healthy.name: Healthy Potato
Potato___healthy.description: The potato plant is healthy, featuring robust leafy stems and healthy root structures.
Potato___healthy.symptoms: None. Leaves are green, broad, and free from target spots or white mold.
Potato___healthy.prevention: Hill potatoes properly, practice 3-year crop rotations, and use drip irrigation to keep foliage dry.

Raspberry___healthy.name: Healthy Raspberry
Raspberry___healthy.description: The raspberry plant is healthy, with upright growth, dark green leaves, and clear canes.
Raspberry___healthy.symptoms: None. Green serrated leaves with no rust spots or cane lesions.
Raspberry___healthy.prevention: Prune old fruited floricanes in autumn, maintain trellises for air flow, and mulch around the base.

Soybean___healthy.name: Healthy Soybean
Soybean___healthy.description: The soybean crop is healthy, with dense, clean green foliage and normal seed pod production.
Soybean___healthy.symptoms: None. Clear green trifoliate leaves without yellow margins or spots.
Soybean___healthy.prevention: Optimize planting densities, rotate crops annually, and ensure proper seed inoculation.

Squash___Powdery_mildew.name: Squash Powdery Mildew
Squash___Powdery_mildew.description: A fungal disease causing a powdery white coating on squash leaves, reducing photosynthesis and yield.
Squash___Powdery_mildew.symptoms: Talcur-powder-like white spots that grow to cover entire leaf surfaces, stems, and petioles; leaves turn yellow and dry.
Squash___Powdery_mildew.causes: Fungus that thrives in dry, warm conditions with high humidity, spreading via wind.
Squash___Powdery_mildew.treatment: Spray horticultural oils, neem oil, or fungicides like potassium bicarbonate at first appearance.
Squash___Powdery_mildew.prevention: Select resistant squash varieties; plant in full sun; space plants out to improve air circulation.

Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.name: Strawberry Leaf Scorch
Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.description: A fungal disease of strawberry leaves that causes purplish spots, leading to leaves drying and appearing scorched.
Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.symptoms: Numerous small, purplish spots on leaves that merge, turning the leaf tissue brown, paper-dry, and curled.
Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.causes: Fungal spores that overwinter on infected leaves and spread in wet conditions during spring.
Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.treatment: Apply fungicides during early spring growth and repeat if damp weather persists.
Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.prevention: Remove old leaves after harvest; keep plant rows narrow to facilitate quick drying; plant resistant varieties.

Strawberry___healthy.name: Healthy Strawberry
Strawberry___healthy.description: The strawberry plant is healthy, showing bright green trifoliate leaves and healthy runners.
Strawberry___healthy.symptoms: None. Foliage is clean, green, and free from purple spots or margins.
Strawberry___healthy.prevention: Mulch with clean straw, prune runners if dense, and water at soil level.

Tomato___Bacterial_spot.name: Tomato Bacterial Spot
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.description: A bacterial disease causing spots on leaves, stems, and fruit, resulting in defoliation and sunburned tomato crop loss.
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Small, dark, circular lesions with yellow halos on leaves; raised black scabs on tomato fruits.
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.causes: Bacteria carried on seeds or overwintering in plant debris, spreading in warm, wet weather.
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.treatment: Apply copper sprays combined with mancozeb to help manage bacterial spreads early in the season.
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.prevention: Use certified disease-free seeds; avoid overhead watering; rotate crops with non-solanaceous plants.

Tomato___Early_blight.name: Tomato Early Blight
Tomato___Early_blight.description: A common fungal disease causing circular spots with concentric rings on older tomato leaves.
Tomato___Early_blight.symptoms: Dark spots with concentric target-like rings on lower leaves; leaves turn yellow and drop off.
Tomato___Early_blight.causes: Fungal pathogen overwintering in crop residues and soil, splashing up onto leaves during rain.
Tomato___Early_blight.treatment: Apply copper or chlorothalonil fungicides at the first sign of symptoms.
Tomato___Early_blight.prevention: Prune lower leaves to prevent contact with soil; apply thick organic mulch; practice crop rotations.

Tomato___Late_blight.name: Tomato Late Blight
Tomato___Late_blight.description: A highly destructive water-mold disease that can defoliate tomato plants and rot fruit in cool, damp weather.
Tomato___Late_blight.symptoms: Large, dark gray-green spots on leaves that turn black; white fuzzy mold on leaf undersides in wet weather; large brown patches on fruit.
Tomato___Late_blight.causes: Airborne spores of an oomycete pathogen that thrives in cool, wet environments.
Tomato___Late_blight.treatment: Apply preventative fungicides immediately when weather conditions turn wet and cool; remove infected plants.
Tomato___Late_blight.prevention: Ensure wide spacing for air flow; avoid watering leaves; select late-blight resistant tomato cultivars.

Tomato___Leaf_Mold.name: Tomato Leaf Mold
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.description: A fungal leaf disease common in greenhouse tomatoes, causing leaf yellowing and defoliation under high humidity.
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.symptoms: Pale green or yellow spots on upper leaf surfaces; olive-green velvety fungal growth on the leaf underside.
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.causes: Fungus that thrives in warm, highly humid (relative humidity > 85%) greenhouse environments.
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.treatment: Apply sulfur or copper fungicides; increase ventilation in greenhouses.
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.prevention: Maintain greenhouse humidity below 85%; prune lower leaves to increase air flow; water early in the day.

Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.name: Tomato Septoria Leaf Spot
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.description: A very common fungal leaf spot disease of tomatoes, starting on lower leaves and moving upwards.
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.symptoms: Numerous small, circular spots with dark borders and tan-to-gray centers containing tiny black dots (fruiting bodies).
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.causes: Fungus that survives in crop debris and weeds, spreading via splashing water from rain or hose.
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.treatment: Apply protective fungicides regularly during wet weather; prune lower foliage.
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.prevention: Mulch the soil; rotate crops; clear out tomato vines at the end of the season; avoid overhead watering.

Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.name: Tomato Spider Mites
Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.description: Tiny arachnid pests that feed on plant leaf sap, causing speckling, yellowing, and leaf death in hot, dry conditions.
Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.symptoms: Fine yellow speckling on leaves; fine webbing on the undersides of leaves and growing tips; leaves turn bronze and dry.
Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.causes: Pest outbreak promoted by hot, dusty, dry conditions that reduce natural predators.
Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.treatment: Apply insecticidal soaps, neem oil, or miticides; blast plants with water to dislodge mites.
Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.prevention: Keep plants well-watered; spray down paths to reduce dust; encourage beneficial insects like ladybugs.

Tomato___Target_Spot.name: Tomato Target Spot
Tomato___Target_Spot.description: A fungal disease affecting tomato leaves, stems, and fruit, resembling early blight but with smaller lesions.
Tomato___Target_Spot.symptoms: Small, circular spots with light brown centers and dark rings (target shape); fruit develops sunken, circular lesions.
Tomato___Target_Spot.causes: Fungus that overwinters in plant debris and grows in warm, humid weather.
Tomato___Target_Spot.treatment: Apply copper-based or systemic fungicides early when symptoms appear.
Tomato___Target_Spot.prevention: Remove crop residue; ensure adequate plant spacing; avoid overhead irrigation.

Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.name: Tomato Yellow Leaf Curl
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.description: A destructive viral disease causing leaf curling, stunting, and complete failure to produce fruit.
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.symptoms: Severe stunting of the plant; leaves curl upward and inward, developing yellow margins and smaller leaf sizes.
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.causes: Viral pathogen transmitted by the silverleaf whitefly (Bemisia tabaci) insect vector.
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.treatment: No chemical treatment is available. Remove and destroy infected plants immediately.
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.prevention: Use whitefly-proof netting; apply insecticides or organic treatments to control whiteflies; grow resistant varieties.

Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.name: Tomato Mosaic Virus
Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.description: A highly infectious virus that mottles leaves and stunts growth, easily spread mechanically by hands and tools.
Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.symptoms: Mottling of leaves with alternating light and dark green areas (mosaic pattern); leaf distortion (shoestring leaves); fruit discoloration.
Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.causes: Highly stable virus spread by mechanical contact, contaminated tools, seeds, or hands (especially smokers due to tobacco virus ties).
Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.treatment: No cure. Remove and burn infected plants. Wash hands and sterilize tools in non-fat dry milk solution.
Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.prevention: Buy certified virus-free seeds; sanitize pruning shears between plants; avoid handling plants after using tobacco.

Tomato___healthy.name: Healthy Tomato
Tomato___healthy.description: The tomato plant is healthy, showing bright green foliage, robust stems, and clean, glossy fruit.
Tomato___healthy.symptoms: None. Green, flat leaves with no spots, curls, or fuzzy mold.
Tomato___healthy.prevention: Provide support (cages or stakes), water consistently at the base, and prune suckers to promote air circulation.
